text:
alex_support: customer ACME reporting streaming sessions marked as 5xx and billed; says client saw 'broken pipe' after ~3s, but response body contains valid chunked data up to that point. request_id=req_0a9f3b, region=us-west-2. escalating because they got charged for the failed tokens.

customer_acme_dev: yep, we get repeated truncation. our client reconnects and resumes fine. sample curl we use:
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=rm-small\
  --no-buffer
```
we see chunk-trailers sometimes missing and then socket close.

alex_support: thanks — assigning to oncall, adding logs. @emily_oncall can you pick this up? cc @jordan_sre for metric effects.

emily_oncall: on it. can you paste gateway logs and metric tags? curious if we saw FIN vs RST from upstream.

alex_support: paste of gateway excerpt (truncated):
```
[2026-03-10T14:03:12Z] req=req_0a9f3b client=10.4.5.6 proxy_write: wrote 1024/1024 chunk, flushed
[2026-03-10T14:03:15Z] req=req_0a9f3b proxy_read: upstream closed connection (code=RST)
[2026-03-10T14:03:15Z] req=req_0a9f3b classify: labeled as 5xx (upstream failure) tokens_billed=120
```

jordan_sre: interesting — kernel-level RST vs client-initiated FIN is what changes billing classification. does gateway distinguish half-close (FIN) vs abort (RST)? historically we flagged RST as upstream error (5xx). if client sends FIN and stops reading, that's a client abort and shouldn't be billed.

lee_platform: current heuristic: if any upstream-side connection close before trailer, we mark as 5xx unless we observed a graceful halfclose sequence and app-level EOF. But we know some proxies (company VPNs, winhttp) send RST on idle-client sockets. leads to false positives.

emily_oncall: can we repro locally? steps: run a small node client that stops reading after N chunks, and see what gateway logs. I can try. @alex_support can you ask ACME for a PCAP or client-side logs showing socket flags?

customer_acme_dev: attaching client logs (excerpt):
```
[14:03:12] recv chunk size=1024
[14:03:13] processed chunk
[14:03:14] app crashed, closed socket abruptly (we're shipping a fix)
[14:03:14] tcp: socket closed by app -> FIN? our runtime shows RST to peer
```
we're not certain which side generated RST.

alex_support: ACME says their app crashed, so likely client-side abrupt close. they still dispute billing because they expect no charge for incomplete streams.

sam_billing: billing note: we only bill emitted tokens. our pipeline currently marks this req as 5xx and retains billed tokens due to safety of upstream errors. if we reclassify as client-abort we need to drop billing, but this affects aggregated metrics and quota accounting.

jordan_sre: proposal: add a short reconciliation step for streaming sessions where final socket close flags indicate client abort (app-level abrupt close) and where gateway observed successful chunk writes earlier. If conditions match, mark as client_abort and send billing-cancel event. We should add a retention window of 24h for audit.

lee_platform: implement: 1) change classifier to prefer FIN+no-server-error as client abort; 2) add a fallback rule for RST if preceding N seconds include client-side writes and no upstream error codes; 3) emit debug tag streaming_close_cause={fin,rst,unknown} to metrics and traces.

emily_oncall: I'll run a quick repro across linux/WinHTTP paths and put results in the incident ticket. early ask: can engineering create a safe rollout toggled-by-flag for 1) metrics tags and 2) billing reclass? keep default behavior unchanged until we validate.

alex_support: replied to customer: 'we see an abrupt client-side close in your logs which may explain the RST; we're investigating classification and will follow up about billing within 24h. thank you for patience.' :thumbsup:

opsbot: incident created INC-2026-327 (priority=high) assigned to emily_oncall, watchers: jordan_sre, lee_platform, sam_billing.

emily_oncall: quick triage update: reproduced with a small node script that calls res.destroy() after 3 chunks — gateway shows RST and current classifier marks 5xx. patch notes prepared to add streaming_close_cause tag. next: instrument billing pipeline for conditional cancellation.

sam_billing: hold any automatic refunds until we confirm mass impact. we can do ad-hoc credits for ACME in parallel.

alex_support: ACME accepted ad-hoc credit pending system fix. closing loop once we ship classifier toggle.

jordan_sre: follow-ups: add e2e test for client-abort scenario, add unit for kernel-flag logic, and schedule postmortem to decide default heuristics.

alex_support: thanks team — keeping thread open for updates.
